source_observations.section: Noun, formal or polite asking and the thing asked for; email-request examples.
source_observations.finding: The noun can describe an act of asking or the thing asked for. The register tendency and written-message use support the original definition and retained sent-request example. The verb and machine-service request are outside this decision.

source_observations.section: COBUILD countable noun sense3, distinct from the requesting verb.
source_observations.finding: The selected countable noun is polite or formal asking for an action. Its displayed level is B1+. The selected POS is the noun, not the adjacent verbs.

source_observations.section: Countable, usually plural direction/order sense2; contrasts with plural instructions sense1, computer sense3 and teaching sense4.
source_observations.finding: The countable entry describes something a person is told to do and marks it usually plural. Separate sections cover detailed how-to information, computer operations and teaching. This supports the single-direction definition and each instruction example.

source_observations.section: COBUILD countable direction/order sense1; plural how-to sense3.
source_observations.finding: The countable direction or order is separate from the plural how-to information entry. A2 is displayed for that plural entry, not the selected countable direction. The teaching sense is also distinct.

source_observations.section: Formal countable/uncountable noun entry, lines101-114; exclude word-of-day footer.
source_observations.finding: The noun covers making something clearer or easier to understand, and both countable and uncountable use are marked. This directly supports the selected explanation sense and ask for clarification grammar.

source_observations.section: Clarification derived noun under clarify; understanding sense rather than removal of impurities.
source_observations.finding: The derived noun is connected to making a statement or matter clearer. This is supporting derivative evidence, weaker than an independent learner noun entry; Oxford supplies the direct noun and countability evidence. No noun level is claimed.

source_observations.section: Countable noun for a sentence, phrase or word seeking information.
source_observations.finding: The selected noun is used to ask for information. Its grammar supports a question about a topic. Other doubt, problem and verb senses are not being reviewed.

source_observations.section: COBUILD countable information-question noun.
source_observations.finding: The information-request noun has A1. Questioning or doubting as a verb is distinct and its B2 labels are excluded from the noun decision.

source_observations.section: Spoken/written/action response noun and separate exam/correct-answer material.
source_observations.finding: The response entry does not require that an answer provide all requested information. Its broader coverage includes action, but this teaching candidate deliberately selects verbal or written replies to questions.

source_observations.section: COBUILD countable response noun sense2.
source_observations.finding: The selected reply noun is A1. Adjacent answering verbs and replying to a letter are different POS or uses. A response need not be a correct solution.

source_observations.section: Say/write-again entry, contrasted with emphatic and doing-again uses.
source_observations.finding: The lexical evidence includes saying something again. The selected ID and original example choose speech; no approval is extended to all written repetition or repeated actions.

source_observations.section: COBUILD say/write-again verb sense1, lines224-235.
source_observations.finding: A2 is displayed for saying or writing again. The same-spoken-message use is within that sense. Repeating an action is separate even though its entry also displays A2.

source_observations.section: Make understandable verb; explain which/how and explain something to somebody patterns.
source_observations.finding: The entry supports making information understandable and the embedded-question construction in the original example. The recipient is introduced with to when explicitly expressed.

source_observations.section: COBUILD explain sense1, lines224-228.
source_observations.finding: The selected giving-details or describing-to-enable-understanding use displays A2. Other accounting-for or justification uses should not be inferred from this focused teaching decision.

source_observations.section: Examine correctness/safety/acceptability verb entry.
source_observations.finding: The selected use examines whether something is correct or satisfactory. Other verification patterns and homographs require their own context; the original details example fits the selected verb.

source_observations.section: COBUILD checking information/document verb sense1, lines224-237.
source_observations.finding: The selected examine-for-correctness verb displays A2. The inspection noun is B1, while marking a box is a distinct US verb use also marked A2. These adjacent labels do not collapse senses or POS.

source_observations.section: Advice/instructions section sense5, lines202-220; separate accept/copy section follows.
source_observations.finding: The selected transitive verb acts on advice or instructions. Its Suggestions and advice topic displays A2. Copying an example, physical direction, and time order appear in separate sections.

source_observations.section: COBUILD advice/instruction/recipe sense12, lines322-328.
source_observations.finding: The selected acting-as-directed use displays B1. This differs from the Oxford selected A2 label and is kept literal. Movement, sequence and understanding uses do not decide this placement.

source_observations.section: Selected arrangement/official-certainty sense2, lines151-164: reservation and meeting examples with Topics Discussion and agreement B2 at line164. Contrast truth/evidence sense1 Scientific research B1 at line135 and religious sense4 C2 at line170.
source_observations.finding: The selected section makes an arrangement definite or official. Its reservation and meeting examples are followed by the Discussion and agreement B2 topic label. The original null observation omitted that selected label. B1 belongs to the distinct truth/evidence section; neither that label nor a footer label is the selected arrangement evidence.

source_observations.section: COBUILD arrangement or appointment sense3, lines256-260.
source_observations.finding: The selected verb states an arrangement is definite and displays B1+. Evidence and assertion-of-truth senses display B2; the derived confirmation noun also has its own B2 label.
